about: The review of each map's exact bytes (docs/decisions/0017-a-map-change-carries-a-review-of-its-bytes.md). tools/check-map-review.py fails any map whose sha256 is not the one recorded here.

notStaged.reason: This run predates `tools/mapper stage` (#223). Its inputs were staged by hand and were not committed, so there is nothing to hold to a digest: unlike trials 7 and 8, which each wrote a blind-mapping/REDACTIONS.md, this directory has no record of what the second mapper was given. What can be said is what blind-mapping/README.md says -- the mapper was given the pinned extract and had not seen Map A -- and that rests on the runner's word, which is exactly the gap #223 is about. It is recorded here rather than left blank so that the one blind-second-mapping review this repository currently rests on says out loud that its inputs cannot be checked.

firstMap.note: Map A, the first mapping, and the map these bytes are the correction of. It was this example's corpus-map.json under the `legacy` exemption until the reconciled map was promoted to that name (#8); it is frozen evidence now, beside Map B, and carries no review of its own for the reason Map B carries none -- it is an input to this comparison, not a map this repository uses. It is a file and not only a git object because blind-mapping/build-map-c.py reads it: `--check` rebuilds these bytes from it and the resolutions on every validate.sh run, so a correction nobody ruled on fails the gate, and the digest above is the same one compared.sha256 names.

blindMap.note: Map B, copied verbatim from the mapper's bundle with its corpus-manifest.json, and not edited. It is evidence, not a map this repository uses, so it carries no review of its own and is not named by the glob that requires one.

corpus-map.json.scope: Every disagreement results.json flagged has a ruling in resolutions.json. The last one recorded open, worked-examples-as-entries (#216), was ruled on 2026-09-17 by rules-factory decision 0031 and the row carries that ruling beside its original: these bytes differ from the reviewed ones by that row alone, applied by blind-mapping/build-map-c.py, which validate.sh re-runs. What it adds is short-temporary-absences.ambiguity.bounds -- the two (c)(4) examples the blind second mapping and the adjudication both read, with their citations and their verbatim text, which the locator checker holds to the corpus -- and the question it rewrote no longer re-quotes them. No entry's scope, kind, clarity or fate moved. Since then a second change, departing from sha256 5106bb4879b7c1af5fc0ddb1699800e91cd9fb97bada74f483c9ae4dbed83879: docs/decisions/0059 drops the schema exclusion that kept `definedElsewhere` off an entry carrying an `ambiguity` block, and `method-of-allocation` -- which deferred `depreciation adjustments` to section 1250(b)(3) as a `crossReferences[].unmapped` reason, saying in that reason it did so only because of the exclusion -- now declares `definedElsewhere: usc-26-1250`, drops the stand-in, and returns MissingRulesData instead of RequiresInterpretation. `depreciation-not-excludable` has always declared the same statute for the same term that way. No reading of the corpus moves: evidence, scope, clarity, `ambiguity.question` and `ambiguity.fate` are byte-identical; what moves is the runtime reason, by the correspondence table's row order, so this is **not** a non-semantic change and it carries an independent verdict rather than an exemption. That is independent-verdict-218-226.json, which names these bytes. Applied by blind-mapping/build-map-c.py as a **schema migration**, a second kind of step beside the adjudication rulings: Map A is frozen trial evidence and is not edited to follow the schema, so the migration is keyed to the decision record and counted apart from the rows. The reviewer disagreed twice over two rounds and both were acted on: it found that the entry's question names (e)(4) Example 6 as the case where no method exists and that Example 6 is a no-allocation case under (e)(1), which is filed as #407 and not corrected here, and it held that the change must not rest on the same mistake -- so the note now states the gap on the face of (e)(3), names #407, records that the deleted item's claim about the schema was true when written, carries forward that item's reference to finding 4, and says that admitting section 1250(b)(3) would oblige splitting the entry.
